problem_description: Compute the average potential energy per particles in eV for a bimetallic Ag-Cu nanoparticle. The system should have 309-atom Mackay icosahedral cluster. Interatomic interactions were described using the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) alloy potential, with parameters corresponding to Ag and Cu atoms. The simulations should be carried out in metal units with periodic boundary conditions applied in all three spatial directions. The timestep was set to 0.001 ps. Initial atomic velocities were assigned according to a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at 300 K. And, again the system should equilibrated in the NVT ensemble using a Nose-Hoover thermostat, where the temperature was gradually increased from 150 K to 950 K over a simulation time of 100,000 steps. After heating, the system should cooled from 950 K to 300 K under the NVT ensemble for another 100,000 steps. The system should further equilibrated at a constant temperature of 300 K for 100,000 steps in the NVT ensemble. A semi-grand canonical Monte Carlo (SGCMC)-like atom swap algorithm should employed using the fix atom/swap command where kinetic energy in not included in swapping (ke no). During this stage, Ag and Cu atom types needs to be allowed to exchange positions at a fixed temperature of 300 K. The swap dynamics were performed for 100,000 steps, allowing the system to approach chemical equilibrium.
